title: RoutingDecision
description: One canonical typed boundary for a routing recommendation, owned by the Kernel. A routing decision is a recommendation and its complete rationale. It confers no authority: reading one grants nothing, and `authorizes` is required to be null so the absence is asserted rather than assumed. Organ adapters CONSUME this contract; they do not copy it into a parallel shape. Ratified by FOUNDER-RULING-2026-08-22 ruling 4 (DEC-OM-001).

contract.description: The capability or contract this decision routes for

consequence_class.description: The consequence class of the request being routed, in the institution's ONE canonical vocabulary — the same values used by policy.engine, capabilities.genome, discovery.service and every organs/*.manifest.yaml. A candidate whose authority ceiling is below this is removed from consideration, never merely down-ranked. The first draft of this schema invented a parallel set (internal/reversible/external); it is recorded here because a second consequence vocabulary is exactly the parallel contract this ruling forbids, and it would have type-checked cleanly while meaning something different to every other component.

selected.description: The chosen candidate, or null. Null is a valid FINAL answer meaning no candidate may serve this request — not an invitation to retry with weaker criteria.

ranking.description: Every eligible candidate with its score and breakdown, so a reader can reconstruct why the selection was made rather than trusting it.

breakdown.description: Per-criterion contribution. Present so a decision can be audited without re-running the scorer.

refused.description: Candidates removed from consideration, each with its reason. A decision that reported only the winner would hide the refusals, which are the part worth reviewing.

criteria.description: The weights actually applied, carried with the decision. A decision whose weights are not recorded cannot be compared against a later one.

weights_are_declared_not_learned.description: True while the weights are hand-chosen rather than fitted to outcomes. Cannot become false until real outcomes exist to fit them; until then, presenting a router as outcome-optimised would be a claim the institution has not earned. See FOUNDER-RULING-2026-08-22: architectural selection today must not be misrepresented as evidence that one router produces better outcomes.

authorizes.description: Always null, and required. A routing decision is not a capability grant, a budget, an approval or an execution right. Typed as null rather than omitted so that any future attempt to carry authority through this boundary fails schema validation instead of passing silently.

grants_issued.description: Always exactly zero, and typed as a const rather than a minimum. A router that issued one grant would be a router that authorised, and this boundary makes that a schema violation instead of a code review finding.

selected_origin.description: Where the selected implementation came from. Recorded for audit and NEVER an input to selection — a mechanism must not win for resembling a metaphor nor lose for being conventional. The scorer cannot read it; see capabilities.implementations.Implementation.selectable_view.
